title: Bind private-beta release provenance before upload
summary: Bind private-beta version, tag, source commit, release channel state, and asset replacement policy before any GitHub Release upload.
reason: Remediate AUDIT-FIND-W10-013, which permits independently valid version/tag inputs and unconditional clobber of assets on an existing release without proving its commit or channel identity.
behavior_before: Private-beta release inputs were checked only for shape, and an existing release could receive clobbered assets without proving tag/version, target commit, title, or prerelease identity.
behavior_after: Private-beta publication requires one bound version/tag/commit/channel identity; existing versioned assets remain immutable unless a separately explicit same-commit rebuild policy is satisfied.
tests_added: Mismatched version/tag identity is rejected before any remote query or updater metadata write.
A new release binds --target to the full workflow source SHA and uploads without clobber.
An existing tag or release on a different SHA is rejected without create or upload mutation.
Existing same-commit missing assets upload without clobber, while colliding versioned assets remain immutable by default.
Asset clobber is reachable only when explicit same-commit rebuild input and protected environment approval are both present.
Existing release title and channel/prerelease mismatches fail before mutation, and package-mode workflow metadata omission is explicit.
manual_validation: The complete private-beta tooling selection passed 48 tests; the focused publication suite passed 9 isolated fake-GitHub scenarios without network or GitHub mutation.

PowerShell parsing, workflow YAML parsing, GitHub audit-spine hardening, touched Python Ruff and compileall, risky-file registry, test-subsystem inventory, architecture, naming, and god-file checks passed; god-file output contained warnings only.

A full Windows release build with -Zip -Verify -IncludeTests copied 18,436 files and ran for 900 seconds. Package policy, environment, Tauri prerequisites, tool integration, and end-to-end smoke passed; aggregate verification exited 1 only on established WebView static-asset, dependency-cycle, generated/status-document, tracked-office-document, and unrelated Ruff baselines.

A fresh exact release-policy copy matched all 10 included implementation/test/document paths by SHA-256 and passed 18 packaged provenance tests with two expected skips because .github workflow metadata is intentionally omitted from release packages.
rollback_plan: Revert the provenance-binding workflow, release scripts, focused tests, generated artifacts, documentation, and packet metadata together. Do not restore unverified --clobber behavior for versioned assets.
notes: High-risk release gate. Validation used a disposable fake GitHub CLI and release/ref JSON in isolated temporary directories; no remote publication, GitHub release mutation, tag creation, asset upload, signing, live config, lifecycle action, or media access occurred. Python impact is test-only. Existing overlapping batch-020 edits in the workflow, preflight, preflight tests, and private-beta documentation were preserved. Known unrelated worktree baselines remain outside this packet: stale generated summaries, DOC005 at the active audit BASELINE reference, the mediapipeline.core.processes to mediapipeline.core.queue dependency cycle, two rename-test Ruff B023 findings, the WebView static-asset reliability assertion, tracked-office-document findings, and generated/status-document drift. Immutable audit evidence remained read-only.
